after further investigation we have identified what could potentially be the root cause of this problem and why this customer and other customers using the wi-fi calling service within pakistan. 

Voice/Data Raw Registration State (DENIED_EM): This is the failure point. Your phone is reaching out over the internet to register with T-Mobile's servers, but the connection is being actively denied or dropped. The Crackdown: Mid-February—specifically beginning on February 17th—marks the exact timeframe when the Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) initiated widespread internet disruptions. Following political unrest, the government blocked access to platforms like X (formerly Twitter) and began a massive, nationwide crackdown on Virtual Private Networks (VPNs). The Firewall (LIMS): To enforce these bans, local ISPs (like PTCL, StormFiber, and Jazz) and the PTA heavily deployed deep packet inspection (DPI) through a national internet firewall. This system is designed to track, throttle, or outright block unauthorized or unregistered encrypted traffic. The Crossfire: Because Wi-Fi Calling relies entirely on an IPsec VPN tunnel, the Pakistani firewall cannot easily distinguish it from a standard commercial VPN trying to bypass local censorship. To the firewall, your phone's connection to T-Mobile looks like unauthorized encrypted traffic.
